home.title: Rupert, the librarian for your documents
home.description: Rupert finds, names and files your scanned documents, right in the folders you already use: on your computer, iCloud Drive, OneDrive or Google Drive. Ask it questions in English, Spanish or German. For Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone and Android. Free and open source.
hero.eyebrow: Free for Mac, Windows, Linux, iPhone and Android
hero.lead: Rupert reads every scan, files new ones for you and answers questions about them, right in the folders you already use. Nothing to import. Nothing locked in.
android.hero: Android: an early beta, from this site. Google Play comes later.
android.heading: Rupert for Android is an early beta.
android.detail: It's still being tested, so expect rough edges, and please report what you find. It isn't on Google Play yet, so Google hasn't reviewed it: download it here and open it to install. Your phone asks you to allow installing apps from your browser and may warn about an app from outside Google Play. It reads Google Drive and OneDrive and scans with the camera. It doesn't update itself yet: come back here for new versions.
dn.label: Rupert on a Mac, in light and dark mode
dn.alt: Rupert on a Mac in light mode: a folder of insurance documents as large icons, with the selected document's title, date and tags
dn.handle: Drag to compare light and dark mode
dn.caption: Rupert follows your system's light or dark mode. Drag the handle to see both.
ask.h2b: He answers in it, and dresses for it.
ask.p: Ask for a document in plain words. Rupert searches your library, reads what he finds and shows it in the window. He speaks English, Spanish and German, and so does the rest of the app.
ask.tick1: Runs on your computer with Local AI (LM Studio, Ollama and the like), or with Claude or ChatGPT if you choose.
ask.tick2: Reads, finds and shows. Never renames, moves or deletes.
every.lead: The same sidebar, the same search, the same inbox on every computer. Only the window's frame changes. On your phone, the same folders with the same titles and tags.
every.altDesktop: Rupert's window: the Insurance folder as large icons, with the selected document's details
every.altPhone: Rupert on iPhone: the same Insurance folder with the same titles, dates and tags
every.altAndroid: Rupert on Android: the same Insurance folder with the same titles, dates and tags
every.note.mac: On a Mac, in the Finder's folders, iCloud Drive, OneDrive and Google Drive.
every.note.win: On Windows, with OneDrive and Google Drive's streaming drive, without downloading your whole Drive.
every.note.linux: On Linux as an AppImage, .deb or .rpm, with any folder you sync.
every.note.phone: On iPhone, read from iCloud Drive, OneDrive or Google Drive. Text and titles come from your computer.
every.note.android: On Android (early beta), read from Google Drive or OneDrive, with scans from the camera. Download it here; Google Play comes later.
scan.altPhone: Rupert on iPhone: the Scan tab, where tapping the owl starts the camera
scan.altMac: Rupert's inbox on a Mac: a new scan of an electricity bill, with the suggested title, date and tags filled in
scan.s1: Tap the owl. The camera finds the page's edges; add as many pages as you like.
scan.s2: It lands in your inbox, one PDF in iCloud Drive, OneDrive or Google Drive.
scan.s3: Rupert reads it on your computer and suggests a title, date, tags and folder.
scan.s4: One click files it, renamed, with its details written into the PDF.
more.h2: Everything else a good librarian does
more.folders.p: Add the folders you already keep documents in. Rupert shows them as they are, moves documents between them when you ask, and keeps up with every change, whether you make it in Rupert, the Finder or File Explorer.
more.find.p: Every word of every PDF, with the matches highlighted. Accents don't matter.
more.travel.p: Titles, tags, dates and notes are saved inside the PDF, so they go wherever the file goes.
more.online.p: Files kept in the cloud are listed and searched without downloading them.
more.scanners.p: Scan from AirScan scanners on your network, straight into the inbox.
more.private.p: No account with us, no tracking, no ads. Text recognition and filing suggestions run on your computer, and Rupert is open source, so anyone can check.
more.scansnap.p: Bring over its dates, favorites, receipts and recognized text, without moving a file.

dl.note: For your computer, from Rupert's releases on GitHub.
dl.mac.req: macOS 13 or later · Apple silicon and Intel
dl.mac.choice: On a Mac, pick one: the .dmg from GitHub updates itself; the Mac App Store edition is updated by the App Store.
dl.ios.req: iOS 16 or later · scan, browse and search
dl.android.req: Early beta · Android 7 or later, with Google Play services
dl.fine: All downloads, checksums and release notes are on GitHub. Optional: a Local AI app such as LM Studio or Ollama for filing suggestions and Ask Rupert; on Windows and Linux, Tesseract for text recognition.
support.title: Rupert support
support.description: Help with Rupert, the librarian for your documents: the built-in help, reporting a problem, and ideas.
support.inapp.p: On a computer, Rupert's help covers every feature: Help ▸ Rupert Help, or press F1. It explains adding folders, the inbox, scanning, online-only files, Ask Rupert and setting up AI models, and the phone app.
support.report.p: Please open a bug report on GitHub. The form asks for what's needed to look into it:
support.report.version: Rupert's version: on a computer it's shown at the bottom left of the window; on a phone in Rupert's Settings ▸ About.
support.report.system: Your system and its version (for example macOS 15, Windows 11, iOS 18 or Android 15), and your device.
support.report.steps: What happened, what you expected, and the steps that lead to it.
support.report.private: Please leave out private document contents, account details and API keys from screenshots and logs.
support.ideas.p: Suggestions are welcome as a feature request on GitHub. You can also see what's being worked on.
support.privacy.p: Rupert collects nothing about you. The privacy policy explains what happens to your information. Questions about privacy: contact@rupertlibrarian.com.
